annotations.text:
SELLING — the four screens that make the money

The run is: see who is worth a visit, find the thing, price it, send it.

WHAT HE EARNS IS ON EVERY LINE. The app today shows a floor price and leaves him to work his own cut out in his head. Every product row now carries "3,800 to you", and a promoted line carries "+2,500 to you" in the brand red. He can see which shelf pays him.

ADDING AN ITEM IS THE SCREEN THAT DECIDES WHAT HE MAKES, so it is the best screen in the set. He sets the price himself, the margin moves as he sets it, and a gauge says where he stands between the shop's price to him and the top of what it expects — competitive, or about to lose the sale. agent-catalog already computes ourPrice for exactly this guidance and nothing ever showed it.

THE ORDER RIDES WITH HIM. A dark bar at the foot of the selling screen carrying the total AND his cut, so it is never scrolled away while he adds to it. At the close the tally goes dark like the earnings hero and his earnings are the largest figure on the screen.

Every name on these screens truncates with an ellipsis and carries its full value in a title. No figure ever truncates — a clipped price is a wrong price, and "1,240,00" is a tenth of "1,240,000" and looks entirely plausible.

CLIENTS AND MONEY

DUE AND QUIET ARE HIS CUSTOMERS' OWN RHYTHM, not a rule the shop set. computeOpportunities() already learns each customer's average gap between orders; a client past their own gap is Due, one past sixty days is Quiet. Everyone else is ranked by what they have earned him, because that is the honest measure of a relationship in this job.

ONE CLIENT is built around the fastest sale in the app: what they always buy, already priced, one tap into a new order. Underneath it, their pattern and their payment record — the two things that decide whether to drive out there.

MONEY carries the six-month chart. A month with no orders is a hairline and a dash, never a bar of zero: a zero that looks measured cannot be told from a real one. Past months sit at 2.99:1 against the card and September carries the accent — told apart by hue and by a bold label, never by colour alone, and every bar is directly labelled so the fill is never the only carrier.

ORDERS says where each one actually is, in the shop's words — being packed, ready to collect, delivered and paid, delivered and not paid for twelve days. An order he has sent is out of his hands, and the thing he wants to know is whether it landed and whether he has been paid.

ACCOUNT states his terms as a sentence he can act on, not a badge reading PREPAY that somebody has to have explained to him.

STANDING answers the thing a commission agent actually asks: how am I doing against the others. agent-leaderboard already exists and already draws the line this screen has to hold -- it returns another agent's RANK and NAME (first name, last initial) and never their amount, because what an agent makes is their own income. So the board shows position, and only your own row carries a figure. The screen says so out loud rather than looking like data failed to load.

The nine milestones are the ones agent.html already computes, presented as a number with a word under it instead of nine bespoke badges nobody can tell apart -- earned in the dark, the next one in the accent with its progress, the rest pale. Above them, the single next milestone with the gap named in the units it is measured in: "3 to go" is something to do this week, a locked badge is not.

On Home all of this is ONE row -- rank and streak, one tap away. The old app gave it a health-score card, a flame chip and a nine-badge shelf clipped mid-word, above the work.

THE TARGET IS WIRED IN. 0024_agent_goals.sql has held daily_target and monthly_target since it was written, with a comment saying it drives the progress ring on Home "once that lands". It never landed, so the hero paced against the agent's own best month -- a number he cannot move.

Now the hero paces against a target he set, and turns it into today's job: the month is abstract, "22,000 a day for the 6 days left" is something he can go and do. It also tells him what he is averaging, so the gap is a lift he can size rather than a bar that is simply short.

The sheet takes one number. Because the table holds both columns, he sets whichever he thinks in -- for the month or per day -- and the other is worked out from it. Three presets are drawn from his own history, never a figure the shop picked. And it says out loud that the row is his: the RLS policy is agent_id = current_agent_id(shop_id), so the shop genuinely cannot read it, and an agent who believes that will set an honest number instead of one that looks good.

On day one there is no target and no best month, so there is nothing honest to pace against -- the hero asks for one rather than drawing an empty bar. And the six-month chart carries the same target as a dashed reference line, which is what makes the chart say something rather than just report.

THE TWO STATES THAT DECIDE WHETHER THE APP IS TRUSTED

DAY ONE. A new agent currently meets a 0% health ring and nine locked badges. A zero here is not a failure and the screen must not dress it as one: it says what the number will mean once there is one — "everything you add on top of the shop's price is yours" — and names the single move that starts it. The catalogue is the shop's, so it is already full: there is something to sell before there is anybody to sell it to.

A READ THAT FAILED. The app says "You're offline" for two different problems, and the second one is not offline at all: loadAgentHomeData() sets dataLooksSuspect when a read comes back empty on a session it could not renew. That is a server that did not answer, and telling him to check his wifi is the wrong instruction.

So the banner names which failure it is. The hero states its own figure "as at 6:12am" rather than shouting a stale number as though it were live. Today's orders read "not read yet" — never a zero, because on a money screen a zero that looks measured is the most expensive lie the app can tell. And because nothing in this app sends itself, the screen says plainly that an order built now is checked against the shop's live prices at the moment it is sent, never against these.
